svg.desc: Banner for a paper proving exact worst-case bounds for the difference-of-convex algorithm and proximal gradient. Title: the best constant step for proximal gradient is not 1 over L. Subtitle: exact worst-case guarantee on the gradient mapping, relative to the step 1 over L, for convex problems; higher is better. A chart with the constant stepsize from 0.5 over L to 2 over L on the horizontal axis and the guarantee from 0 to 2 times on the vertical axis; a dashed vertical line marks the textbook step 1 over L, where every curve equals 1 times. Three curves, for N equals 2 (blue), 5 (green) and 20 (amber) iterations, rise to a marked peak and then fall steeply. Right: best constant step for convex problems: about 1.6 over L at N equals 2, 1.48 times better; about 1.75 over L at N equals 5, 1.68 times better; about 1.9 over L at N equals 20, 1.88 times better. A convex proximal term does not change it: the gradient-descent optimum stays optimal. Past the optimum the guarantee falls steeply: 2 percent too long loses about 5 times at N equals 20. Exact worst-case curves from the paper, not experiments. Footer: DCA and proximal gradient: the conjectured exact bounds hold for every N and are attained; unrefereed candidate.
